pass: test-03-correction (no Apify spend). Re-review of already-paid data under the corrected 'Scrolly Reel Opportunity' definition, 2026-09-25
definition: A currently circulating, copyable short-form mechanic (visual action and/or text structure and/or audio) that ordinary creators are recreating now, which a business owner can film in minutes on a phone (<=15s, ideally 5-10s, 1 person, 1-3 shots, no dancing). The business adaptation comes last.
evidenceNote: creatorsInOurData counts distinct creators using the exact sound ID across all 671 already-collected videos. soundCheck figures are from the clockworks sound-scraper runs (top-popular sample, not newest). Nothing here is an Instagram signal: all of it is TikTok data.

examples.name: "-A" text from Pretty Little Liars
examples.label: Circulating (3 creators + trend-account callout)

examples.note: trend-spotting account; on-screen text reads TRENDING SOUND plus instructions

examples.visualMechanic: Hold your phone like a text just arrived, read it, look up at the camera and glance around. One shot, 5-7s.
examples.textMechanic: One snarky, knowing message about what you are doing right now, signed "-A".
examples.audioMechanic: Essential: the PLL sound is what tells viewers which trend this is. Audio risk MEDIUM (TV-show audio may not be available to business accounts).
examples.adaptation: Café: "Third oat latte before 10am? Your secret's safe with me… for now. -A". Salon: "Told her 'just a trim'? We both know it's a full chop. -A"

examples.name: Hands-to-lens reveal
examples.label: Trending

sourceFacts.soundCheck: 7 distinct creators in the last 14 days; 10 of 10 sampled uses at 100K+ plays; first sampled use 2026-08-25

examples.visualMechanic: Close selfie shot in the 'before' state, mouthing along to the audio. Push both hands toward the lens so they fill the frame, then pull away to reveal the 'after' in the same framing.
examples.textMechanic: Optional one-liner: "[Did X] for the first time in [Y] years…"
examples.audioMechanic: Helpful (the beat marks the reveal); substitutable. Audio risk MEDIUM.
examples.adaptation: Stylist: client's hair before → hands → blowout. Product: empty shelf → hands → styled display. Cleaner: cluttered counter → hands → clean.

examples.name: Kick-on-the-beat outfit change
examples.label: Trending

sourceFacts.soundCheck: 5 distinct creators in the last 14 days (snapshot-1 check); 11 creators and 7 recent across our data
sourceFacts.copyingChain: @brookemonk_ (11.7M plays): "I saw @kingapawlik_ do this and had to try"

examples.visualMechanic: Stand in a hallway or room in loungewear. Kick a leg up 2-3 times on the beat, cut on the last kick, and land in the same spot fully dressed, then pose. The camera stays still on a phone stand.
examples.textMechanic: None needed; the caption carries it.
examples.audioMechanic: Essential for the kick timing, though another beat works. Audio risk MEDIUM.
examples.adaptation: Boutique: loungewear → your new-arrivals outfit. Realtor: sweats → showing-day suit, text "open house mode". Local team: street clothes → uniform.

examples.name: Silly face → glam cut
examples.label: Early (2 creators)
examples.visualMechanic: Unready (robe, no makeup) pulling an exaggerated grimace at the camera → hard cut → the finished look, smiling.
examples.textMechanic: Hook text at the top: "This look needed more than just one video 👀"
examples.audioMechanic: Helpful; a 'transition audio' made for this. Audio risk MEDIUM.
examples.adaptation: Nail tech: bare nails + grimace → chrome set. Product: sad plain box → gift-wrapped. Baker: flat dough → finished cake.

examples.name: Bag strap in teeth, duo outfit swap
examples.label: Early (2 creators + 'ib' credit)
examples.visualMechanic: Two people in sweats, each biting a bag strap → cut → both styled, same pose.
examples.adaptation: Boutique owner + friend: day off → styled in the new drop. Two-person service team: day off → on duty.
